subject: Regional proxy deprecation: impact for EU-residency customers & attestation request
messages:
From: EdgeBridge Ops <ops@edgebridge.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: regional-data-proxy (eu-west-1) scheduled deprecation

Hi Vanessa,

Heads up — EdgeBridge will retire the regional-data-proxy instance in eu-west-1 on 2029-10-15 as part of our consolidation plan. We are sending deprecation notices to downstream customers today. The instance currently performs TLS termination and transient buffering for EU-residency tenants.

Attachments: edgebridge_deprecation_notice.pdf (pdf, 240KB)

What this means in practice:
- Traffic currently routed through that proxy will be routed via our global-ingress layer (us-east), which may change egress jurisdictions for a subset of requests.
- We will provide an opt-in onshore routing option but it requires customers to accept new peering details and updated DPA addenda.

If you need a formal subprocessor change notice or a signed attestation describing which data paths will be affected, we can produce that within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Samir Banerjee
Ops Lead, EdgeBridge
ops@edgebridge.com

Vanessa — thanks for the ping. Quick read: most of our customer DPAs define "subprocessor" broadly to include third parties that receive Personal Data on our behalf, which would include EdgeBridge's proxy function. The deprecation and planned routing change will therefore trigger our subprocessor notification flow unless EdgeBridge can demonstrate equivalent onshore handling for EU-residency tenants.

I need two things from Ops/Infra:
1) A table of affected customers + % of traffic that would egress outside EU after cutover.
2) A copy of any attestation EdgeBridge can provide (signed PDF preferred) describing how they will continue to process EU-residency data (onshore routing option or guarantees on transient buffering retention).

I'll draft a short subprocessor-notification email we can send to customers once we have the facts — we should propose a mitigation (onshore peering) and offer a 60-day transition window.

Kim Park
Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Anna — following up with the assessment and next steps. EdgeBridge (our transit subprocessor) has notified us they will deprecate their eu-west-1 regional proxy on 2029-10-15. EdgeBridge has supplied a signed attestation and the option to enable an onshore peering path for impacted tenants.

What we did for FinTrust:
- Runbook: Infra mapped FinTrust tenant egress; ~6% of token requests currently traverse the eu-west-1 proxy and would otherwise egress via us-east. (Jonas attached a dataflow snapshot: dataflow-map-v2.png)
- Mitigation: we requested EdgeBridge enable onshore peering for FinTrust and prepare a DPA addendum; they confirmed this is possible and can be turned on within 7 business days after peering keys are exchanged.
- Timeline: we will send a formal subprocessor-change notice + attestation to FinTrust by 2029-09-20 and offer a 60-day transition window.

Next steps for you: please sign the attached attestation if you accept the onshore peering addendum (link below). If you prefer we keep your traffic on global-ingress (us-east) we will flag that change in your DPA record and provide an updated dataflow report.

Attachments: edgebridge_attestation_signed.pdf (attached by EdgeBridge), dataflow-map-v2.png
Link to DPA addendum draft: https://app.redwood.ai/hubspot/deal/FT-4821

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk the changes.
